title: The transport of cohomology along the geometric Frobenius is an isomorphism
statement:
Fix the finite-field datum [def-weil-finite-field-fiber] $p,a,q,k_0,k$, a
prime $\ell\neq p$, a finite extension $E/\Ql$ contained in the chosen
algebraic closure $\Qlb$, an integer $n\geq1$, and a coefficient ring
$\Lambda\in\{A_{E,n},\mathcal O_E,E,\Qlb\}$. Let $Y_0$ be a separated
finite-type [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties] $k_0$-scheme, put
$Y=Y_0\times_{k_0}k$, $s=\Spec k$, let $a_Y:Y\to s$ be the structure
morphism, let $g_Y:Y\to Y$ be the geometric Frobenius
[def-weil-frobenius-detailed] and $g_s=\Spec(\operatorname{Frob}_q):s\to s$.
Let $\iota_N$ (for $N\in D^b_c(s,\Lambda)$), $\operatorname{FrEx}_{Y,*}(M)$,
$\operatorname{FrEx}_{Y,!}(M)$, $\tau_M$ and $\tau_{c,M}$ (for $M\in
D^b_c(Y,\Lambda)$) be the point transport, the exchange maps along the
Frobenius square, and the transports of ordinary and compactly supported
cohomology along $g_Y$ of [def-weil-frobenius-cohomology-transport]. Then:

1. for every $N\in D^b_c(s,\Lambda)$, $\iota_N:\operatorname{Fib}_s(N)\to
\operatorname{Fib}_s(Lg_s^*N)$ is an isomorphism;

2. for every $M\in D^b_c(Y,\Lambda)$,
$\operatorname{FrEx}_{Y,*}(M):Lg_s^*Ra_{Y*}M\to Ra_{Y*}Lg_Y^*M$ and
$\operatorname{FrEx}_{Y,!}(M):Lg_s^*Ra_{Y!}M\to Ra_{Y!}Lg_Y^*M$ are
isomorphisms in $D^b_c(s,\Lambda)$;

3. consequently, for every $M\in D^b_c(Y,\Lambda)$,
$\tau_M:\RGamma(Y,M)\to\RGamma(Y,Lg_Y^*M)$ and
$\tau_{c,M}:\RGammac(Y,M)\to\RGammac(Y,Lg_Y^*M)$ are isomorphisms, natural
in $M$, and so are the induced maps $\mathrm H^i(\tau_M)$ and
$\mathrm H^i(\tau_{c,M})$ on cohomology groups
[def-weil-ordinary-compact-cohomology] for every integer $i$.

proof.text: For frobeniusCohomologyQbarFunctor_existsUnique, use the canonical stage data and coefficient-enlargement invariance. Define the arrow map by Quotient.lift of B(K,L).hom followed by R_L(f) followed by B(M,L).inv. Eventual equality and the invariance lemma prove well-definedness. Identity follows by functoriality and cancellation; choose a common stage for two arrows to prove composition by cancelling the middle comparisons. Pair hom induction and Functor.hext prove uniqueness. This proves the quotient descent completely from the strictly smaller pre-quotient equality.

Apply [lem-weil-point-automorphism-derived-transport-inverse] with $g=g_s$, an automorphism by [lem-weil-frobenius-square-cartesian]. The specified finite/integral point transport is $t^{g_s}_N$ [def-weil-frobenius-point-transport], so its displayed inverse proves part 1 at these stages. Every integral constructible input is complete by [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed]. At $E$, apply scalar extension to this inverse [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi]; at $\Qlb$, represent it at the same coefficient stage [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients]. Functoriality sends both inverse identities to identities. No idempotent completion is used.

proof.text: For separated finite-type $f_0$ use [lem-weil-frobenius-finite-exchange-inverse] at each finite level, with the retained compactification, and [lem-weil-frobenius-system-exchange-inverse] for the specified integral system maps and their realization. Thus both exchanges of [def-weil-frobenius-square-exchange] are invertible. Their rational and common-stage forms are images of the integral arrows under the functors in that definition: the image of each inverse is an inverse. Taking $f_0=a_{Y_0}$ gives exactly the exchanges of [def-weil-frobenius-cohomology-transport]. Their inverses belong to the full constructible subcategory, proving part 2.

proof.text: By [def-weil-frobenius-cohomology-transport], $\tau_M=\operatorname{Fib}_s(\operatorname{FrEx}_{Y,*}(M))\iota_{Ra_{Y*}M}$, and likewise with $!$ for $\tau_{c,M}$. Hence the inverse is $\iota_{Ra_{Y*}M}^{-1}\operatorname{Fib}_s(\operatorname{FrEx}_{Y,*}(M)^{-1})$, respectively the $!$ formula. The point fibre is a functor [def-weil-finite-coefficient-point]. Compose the point naturality square [lem-weil-frobenius-point-transport-natural] with the natural exchange square [def-weil-frobenius-square-exchange]; this gives naturality of both transports, including every common-stage morphism. Applying the cohomology functor $\mathrm H^i$ [def-weil-ordinary-compact-cohomology] to the two inverse identities and the naturality square proves part 3 for every integer $i$.

proof_origin.place: Deligne, La conjecture de Weil II, (1.1.7) p. 151, (1.1.10)-(1.1.11) pp. 151-152 and (1.1.14) p. 153 state that Gal(k-bar/k) and W(F/F_q) act on fibres, on inverse images and on H^i, H^i_c 'par transport de structure', with no proof that the maps are invertible; the proof (each transport is built from restrictions along automorphisms, the structure isomorphism of an inverse image along an isomorphism, and the mate of an isomorphism along the equivalences Lg^*) is written by an agent; Z6, 2026-10-25: proved the tensor-and-size coefficient tower and coefficient-stage embedding identity in Lean; the transport and descent obligations of the remaining steps are unchanged. F6, 2026-10-25: rational operation scalar comparison is proved by tensor-localizing the specified integral isomorphism; all other remaining transport and descent obligations are retained. U9, 2026-10-26: quotient well-definedness, identity, composition and uniqueness are proved from the pre-quotient coefficient transport equality; the remaining invertibility and naturality statements are unchanged.
